nit:

Since this type appears a lot, what about creating an alias template to avoid template bloat

```
template <
 class Key,
 class T
>
using less_map = std::flat_map<Key, T, std::less<>>;
```

comparison
```
const std::flat_map<std::string, JsonVariantType, std::less<>>&
const less_map<std::string, JsonVariantType>&
```

I'm not sure if it's an enhancement, you can consider it.

I thought about that, but the std::library folks thought this shouldn't be the default, and I don't really want to argue with them 😊

Really, I don't think adding a using declaration helps here, as we really should avoid throwing dicts of keys all over the place.  Sometimes it's needed, but making a using would imply that it's a core type that we want to use a lot of places, and Id' really just prefer we keep it out of api boundaries in the future.

I'd also note that we actually don't want to use the template std::less lookup if the key is not a string, but that gets subtle, and I don't really want to be subtle in a using declaration.
